notes: Sealed held-out briefs for scripts/run_baseline_gate.py. Written by an independent agent on 2026-10-03 and not read by the maintainer while tuning the skill. Open them only for a release decision; once a run on these briefs has informed a change, write a new sealed set.

briefs.prompt: Design the station detail screen for our iOS app for electric-car drivers. Someone has tapped a charging station on the map and needs to decide whether it's worth driving to.
We run a public library app and need a screen where a member can see everything they currently have on loan and when each item is due back. Can you design it?

Map the flow for reporting a broken streetlight in our city services app, which is on iOS and Android. It should start when a resident opens the app on the street and end when they see confirmation that the report was received.

Write a UI spec for the in-run screen of our running app on Android phones. People use it mid-run outdoors, often in direct sunlight, with the phone in an armband or a sweaty hand, glancing at it for a second or two without breaking stride.

We need a UI spec for the attendance screen in our iPad app for primary-school teachers. A teacher marks a class of about 30 pupils present, absent or late at the start of each lesson, sometimes with the iPad flat on the desk in landscape and sometimes holding it in portrait.

Could you review the ticket screen in our Android concert-ticket app for usability and accessibility? The top third is a full-width artist photo with the event name in white 14sp text over it, and right below that the date, venue and seat number share a single line of light grey 11sp text on white. Next comes a row of three unlabelled icon buttons (share, add to calendar, transfer), each 32dp square, and the QR code, about 120dp wide, is last, so on most phones you have to scroll to reach it. The door time appears only as an orange 'Doors open in 2h' chip, and the screen stays at whatever brightness the phone was already set to. No screenshot is available.

Create a typography and spacing system for our live football scores app on iOS and Android. The tricky part is the league table: a team name plus eight numeric columns has to fit across a small phone and still be readable.

Please prepare the design rationale and developer handoff for the redesigned home screen of our weather app. It now opens with the current temperature, a one-line summary and today's high and low, followed by an hourly strip for the next 12 hours and then a 7-day list. The radar map used to sit at the top and has moved to its own tab, and the air quality and UV readings went from two separate cards into one collapsed row under the 7-day list. We removed the video carousel and the lifestyle tips card, and a severe-weather alert now shows as a banner above the temperature only while an alert is active.
